sections.text:
Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion.

FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. Its training-free interface maintains decoded plans between visual predictions. A speed-curvature action buffer is aligned with measured motion at each update, integrated into a local trajectory, and advanced by consuming the current action.

The corrected remainder is written back to the buffer, preserving motion corrections across successive updates. A bounded refresh rule normalizes speed and curvature variations within a newly decoded plan and assigns a short or long reuse budget according to the resulting plan-roughness score.

The interface requires neither backbone features nor an additional learned driving policy.

Over a 3 s horizon, independent real-request evaluation achieves average displacement error (ADE) and final displacement error (FDE) of 0.328/0.596 m on ORAD-3D and 0.266/0.526 m on RELLIS-3D, reducing FDE by 18.0% and 36.7% at request rates of 6.0% and 4.8%, respectively.

These runs retain lower errors across four backbones and both datasets and reduce Qwen3-VL request-processing cost by factors of 16.6 and 20.8 under serial replay, while mechanism and motion-only controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the observed accuracy benefit.

The source code and evaluation materials are publicly available at https://github.com/ADEPT-ORG/FastRoverVLA.

summary.en: FastRoverVLA introduces a training-free interface for off-road vision-language-action driving that separates visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution. It maintains a speed-curvature action buffer, corrects and advances the trajectory using measured motion, and adjusts plan reuse according to plan roughness. In independent real-request evaluation over a 3-second horizon, the authors report displacement errors and request rates on ORAD-3D and RELLIS-3D, with lower errors across four backbones and both datasets. Controls identify persistent state correction as the main source of the accuracy benefit; serial replay also reduces Qwen3-VL request-processing cost.
summary.zh: FastRoverVLA针对越野驾驶VLA模型频繁调用多模态推理、复用计划又无法适应车辆运动变化的问题，提出无需训练的接口，将视觉计划生成与运动条件执行解耦。接口维护速度—曲率动作缓冲区，根据实测运动校正并推进轨迹，再将修正后的剩余动作写回；同时按计划粗糙度设定复用时长。摘要报告其在ORAD-3D和RELLIS-3D上、3秒预测范围内的位移误差与请求率，并称四种骨干网络和两个数据集均保持较低误差；机制对照显示持续状态校正是精度收益的主要来源。串行回放下，Qwen3-VL请求处理成本也有所下降。

items.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving

sections.text:
Vision-Language Models (VLMs) can propose multi-step manipulation plans, but they have no grounded model of how a scene will change, and the pixel-level world models that could check those plans are slow and drift over long horizons.

We present Verify2Act, a modular verification framework that separates semantic action proposal from latent physical verification.

A VLM proposes candidate plans, a latent world model (V2A-WM) imagines each of them in the DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks the imagined rollouts for temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before anything is executed.

V2A-WM extends recent flow-matching world models with cross-attention action grounding and a causal temporal history window. We deploy the full system on a low-cost robot arm, training the world model and critic only on data generated in a digital twin.

Across six language-conditioned tasks, Verify2Act reaches 83.3\% task success, compared with 61.7\% for a latent world model without our architectural changes, 53.3\% for the VLM alone, and 46.7\% for a pixel-diffusion world model.

It verified every plan it executed and incurred no planning-induced failures: all of its failed episodes were caused by low-level grasp or placement slips.

In simulation, Verify2Act obtains the highest five-task chain success on CALVIN among the compared baselines with 30$\times$ fewer reflective VLM calls than pixel-diffusion verification, and the highest success on cluttered nut assembly.

summary.en: Verify2Act separates semantic plan proposal from latent physical verification. A vision-language model proposes manipulation plans, a latent world model imagines their outcomes in DINOv2 feature space, and a dual-head critic checks temporal consistency and goal satisfaction before execution. The system was deployed on a low-cost robot arm, with its world model and critic trained only on digital-twin data. Across six language-conditioned tasks, the authors report higher success than the listed baselines; every executed plan was verified, and failed episodes were attributed to grasp or placement slips. CALVIN and cluttered nut assembly results are from simulation.
summary.zh: Verify2Act将语言条件操作计划的语义提议与潜在物理验证分开：视觉语言模型提出候选计划，潜在世界模型在DINOv2特征空间中预测执行过程，双头评论器检查时间一致性和目标满足情况，再决定是否执行。系统部署于低成本机械臂，世界模型和评论器仅用数字孪生生成的数据训练。在六项任务中，摘要报告其成功率高于所列对照，并称已执行计划均通过验证，失败回合源于抓取或放置滑动。CALVIN多任务链和杂乱螺母装配结果来自仿真。

items.title: Verify2Act: Critic-Guided Latent World Models for Verifying Language-Conditioned Manipulation Plans

sections.text:
Predicting future scene or object states does not necessarily reveal how robot-object interactions will advance or hinder a task. This challenge is particularly pronounced in dynamic robotic manipulation, where objects continue moving during perception and execution.

Effective action generation therefore requires not only modeling object dynamics but also anticipating how future interactions will shape task progress. To this end, we propose \textbf{PhysVAM}, a Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress.

This value-based formulation provides task-directed foresight without reconstructing future visual states. Conditioned on current observations and historical object and robot motion, PhysVAM jointly learns action generation and multi-horizon future-value prediction.

The value branch learns horizon-specific latent representations through future task-value prediction from successful and failed trajectories. These future-value representations are integrated into the action policy through gated cross-attention, guiding action generation toward interactions that facilitate task success.

Extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate superior task success, with absolute success-rate improvements of 27.0 and 27.5 percentage points over the strongest baselines in simulation and real-world tasks, respectively. Project page: https://metarobo.github.io/physvam.github.io/.

summary.en: PhysVAM is a physics-oriented model for dynamic object manipulation that represents anticipated interactions through their effects on future task progress, without reconstructing future visual states. Given current observations and historical object and robot motion, it jointly learns action generation and multi-horizon future-value prediction. A value branch learns horizon-specific latent representations from successful and failed trajectories and feeds them into the policy through gated cross-attention. The authors report superior task success in extensive simulation and real-world experiments, with absolute improvements of 27.0 and 27.5 percentage points over the strongest baselines in those respective settings.
summary.zh: PhysVAM面向动态物体操作，提出以未来任务进展价值表征预期交互的物理导向模型，无需重建未来视觉状态。模型根据当前观测及物体、机器人历史运动，联合学习动作生成与多时间跨度的未来价值预测；价值分支从成功和失败轨迹学习不同时间跨度的潜在表示，并通过门控交叉注意力引导策略选择有助于任务成功的交互。作者称，大量仿真和真实世界实验中，该方法相较最强基线的任务成功率绝对提升分别为27.0和27.5个百分点。

items.title: PhysVAM: Physics-oriented Future Value Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation

sections.text:
Large multimodal models can support long-horizon robot manipulation, but frequent model calls incur substantial latency and token costs. The central challenge is determining when agent assistance or intervention is needed and whether errors require correcting robot execution, subtask planning, or both.

To address this problem, we propose RoC (Reasoning on Call), an efficient framework that coordinates a low-level policy and a high-level reasoning agent through an online task-state monitor. The monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to jointly estimate progress within the active subtask and predict its successor.

These predictions guide event-triggered agent review for coordinated execution repair and plan revision. Verified outcomes govern memory updates and subtask transitions, allowing routine execution to remain with the policy while reasoning focuses on decisions requiring additional assessment.

On RMBench, RoC improves task success rate by 24.0 percentage points and reduces token consumption by 65.3% compared with the strongest agent-based baseline. It also outperforms the strongest policy-based baseline by 15.1 percentage points in task success rate.

Real-world experiments further validate its effectiveness across three long-horizon manipulation tasks. Overall, RoC supports efficient agent intervention and coordinated recovery across execution and planning for long-horizon robot manipulation.

summary.en: RoC (Reasoning on Call) coordinates a low-level policy with a high-level reasoning agent for long-horizon robot manipulation, aiming to limit the latency and token costs of frequent model calls. An online monitor combines temporal visual observations with ordered interaction memory to estimate active-subtask progress and predict the next subtask. These predictions trigger agent review for execution repair, plan revision, or both; verified outcomes guide memory updates and transitions. On RMBench, the authors report a 24.0 percentage-point task-success improvement and 65.3% lower token use than the strongest agent-based baseline. Real-world experiments cover three long-horizon manipulation tasks.
summary.zh: RoC（Reasoning on Call）针对长时程机器人操作中模型频繁调用带来的延迟与成本，协调低层策略和高层推理智能体。在线任务状态监视器结合连续视觉观测与有序交互记忆，估计当前子任务进度并预测下一子任务；这些预测触发智能体审查，以修正执行、调整计划或两者兼顾，并依据已验证结果更新记忆和子任务状态。在RMBench上，作者报告相较最强智能体基线成功率提高24.0个百分点、令牌消耗降低65.3%；真实实验覆盖三项长时程操作任务。

items.title: Reasoning on Call: Efficient Agentic Robot Control for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

sections.text:
Whole-body motion tracking has rapidly expanded the skill repertoire of humanoid robots, yet nearly all of this progress has come from stronger tracking policies, while the motion references they imitate are treated as fixed supervision. We argue that reference quality is a first-order factor in tracking performance.

Human motion data carry capture and estimation artifacts, and retargeting adds physical inconsistencies due to the human-robot embodiment gap; discarding such motions sacrifices valuable skill content, whereas retaining them uncorrected undermines policy learning.

We present RoboForge, a data-centric framework that resolves this dilemma by refining references instead of filtering them, repairing each error in the space where it arises. In human motion space, a quality-guided diffusion model localizes corrupted segments and inpaints only those segments, leaving the rest of the motion intact.

In robot motion space, kinematic repair corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects, and annealed sampling-based optimization under physics rollouts turns kinematically plausible references into dynamically executable ones.

RoboForge requires no change to the tracker: it improves three retargeting methods and four tracking policies, raising the success rate of BeyondMimic from 89.51% to 96.20% while reducing the mean per-joint position error (MPJPE-L) by 31.6%.

Refined references also accelerate policy learning, restore tracking performance from heavily corrupted inputs, and enable more than 30 high-dynamic motions, including flips and the Thomas flare, on a real Unitree G1.

summary.en: The paper presents RoboForge, a framework that improves humanoid whole-body tracking by refining motion references rather than filtering them out. It repairs corrupted segments in human motion space, corrects foot-contact and self-collision defects in robot motion space, and uses optimization under physics rollouts to make references dynamically executable. The authors report improvements across three retargeting methods and four tracking policies without changing the tracker. BeyondMimic success rises from 89.51% to 96.20%, and MPJPE-L falls by 31.6%. They also report over 30 high-dynamic motions on a real Unitree G1.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RoboForge，一种通过修复动作参考而非筛除数据来提升人形机器人全身动作跟踪的框架。它在人体动作空间中定位并修补受损片段，在机器人动作空间中校正足部接触和自碰撞问题，再通过物理仿真优化使动作具备动态可执行性。作者称该方法无需改动跟踪器，可提升三种重定向方法和四种跟踪策略的表现，并加快策略学习、恢复对严重损坏输入的跟踪能力。论文报告 BeyondMimic 成功率由 89.51% 提升至 96.20%，MPJPE-L 降低 31.6%；真实 Unitree G1 上实现了30多种高动态动作。

items.title: RoboForge: Cross-space Motion Refinement for Physically Executable Humanoid Whole-body Tracking

sections.text:
Ferrofluids are liquids containing magnetic nanoparticles, enabling shape control through external magnetic fields. This deformability supports their use as soft robotic bodies that can navigate confined spaces and manipulate objects. Their nonlinear continuum dynamics, however, make reliable control challenging.

Existing work shows how spatial magnetic fields from electromagnet arrays can establish and maintain desired ferrofluid configurations. A complementary objective is to exploit the fluid's dynamics under limited actuation to reach prescribed shapes that may not be sustainable at equilibrium.

Here, we use deep model-based reinforcement learning to control these transient shapes. Learning directly through physical interaction, our policies select current commands for a single fixed electromagnet based on visual observations, guiding the moving ferrofluid toward prescribed geometries.

The learned policies repeatedly attain a variety of shapes spanning polygons, asterisks and pentominoes. These results demonstrate that learning directly from physical interaction enables reliable fluid shaping, opening new possibilities for controlling ferrofluid-based soft robots.

summary.en: The paper studies deep model-based reinforcement learning for controlling transient ferrofluid shapes. From visual observations, a policy selects current commands for a single fixed electromagnet to guide the fluid toward prescribed geometries, including shapes that may not be sustainable at equilibrium. The authors report that policies learned directly through physical interaction repeatedly attain various shapes, including polygons, asterisks, and pentominoes. They present these results as evidence that direct interaction-based learning can enable reliable fluid shaping and may support new forms of control for ferrofluid-based soft robots.
summary.zh: 论文研究利用深度模型式强化学习控制铁磁流体的瞬态形状。方法通过视觉观测让策略为单个固定电磁铁选择电流指令，引导流体形成指定几何形状；目标形状可能无法在平衡状态下维持。作者报告，直接从物理交互中学习的策略能够反复达到多种形状，包括多边形、星形和五连方形。论文将结果视为学习控制流体整形可行性的展示，并指出这为铁磁流体软体机器人的控制提供了可能方向。

items.title: Ferrofluid Shape Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning

sections.text:
Generalist robot policies execute atomic skills reliably but fail when the same skills are composed into long-horizon tasks. Self-improvement from the policy's own experience does not close this gap: experience collected by the policy alone stays within its own distribution and reproduces what it can already do.

We show that what the policy lacks is not a skill but the next step. We present CoachSI, a self-improvement method in which a frozen, off-the-shelf vision-language model (VLM) coaches the policy in language: it watches the robot and names the next step in the format of the policy's atomic instructions, and never outputs an action.

Successful coached rollouts are relabeled in hindsight with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy. The fine-tuned policy is then deployed on its own.

On states where a World Action Model and a Vision-Language-Action model have stalled, naming the next step raises subgoal completion by 4.6x over the unchanged task instruction, and the frozen VLM supplies it from the same camera images the policy sees.

After fine-tuning, unassisted success on long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, 9.8 points above fine-tuning on human demonstrations and 7.3 points above fine-tuning on self-collected successes at an equal data budget. With a coach that sees only camera images, it reaches 56.8%, above both baselines.

The gain is obtained with the action backbone frozen: language coaching teaches the policy what should happen next, and the skills it already has do the rest.

summary.en: The paper introduces CoachSI, in which a frozen vision-language model watches a robot and names the next step in the policy’s atomic-instruction format, without producing actions. Successful coached rollouts are relabeled with the original task instruction and used to fine-tune the policy, which is then deployed without assistance. The authors report 4.6 times higher subgoal completion than the unchanged task instruction in stalled states. On long-horizon tasks in unseen scenes, unassisted success rises from 47.4% to 59.3%, exceeding human-demonstration and self-collected-success fine-tuning baselines at equal data budgets. The action backbone remains frozen.
summary.zh: 论文提出 CoachSI，让冻结的现成视觉语言模型观察机器人，并用语言指出其原子技能策略接下来应执行的步骤，而不输出动作。成功的受指导轨迹随后以原任务指令重新标注，用于微调策略，部署时策略独立运行。作者报告，在特定停滞状态下，指出下一步使子目标完成率达到原任务指令的4.6倍；在未见场景的长时程任务中，无辅助成功率由47.4%升至59.3%，且高于等量数据的人类示范和自采成功轨迹微调基线。方法冻结了动作骨干。

items.title: CoachSI: Self-Improvement of Robot Policies with a Language Coach

sections.text:
Humanoid locomotion research has advanced rapidly on walking and running, but \emph {object-mediated} locomotion, in which a robot must coordinate its body with a passive external object, remains difficult.

One challenging task is skateboarding, which requires simultaneous interaction with the ground and a passive but movable platform to achieve forward motion. Current methods for tackling skateboarding with humanoid robots either require human demonstrations or utilise analytic steering models that require system identification.

In this paper, we introduce a deep reinforcement learning framework that does not rely on prior data such as demonstrations and enables robots such as the K1 humanoid to learn to skateboard using model-free learning. The method combines task rewards with exploit-blocking terminations.

We introduce a number of constraints restricting behaviours such as losing the planted board foot, standing with both feet on the board, excessive twisting, separation from the board, and unstable board motion. Their changing prevalence during training produces an implicit progression from stance control towards sustained robot--board locomotion.

summary.en: The paper presents a model-free deep reinforcement learning framework for teaching a K1 humanoid to skateboard without demonstrations or analytic steering models requiring system identification. It combines task rewards with terminations intended to block exploitative behaviors. Constraints address losing the planted board foot, placing both feet on the board, excessive twisting, separation from the board, and unstable board motion. The authors state that changes in how often these constraints arise during training create an implicit progression from stance control toward sustained robot-board locomotion. The abstract provides no quantitative results.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种无需动作示范或解析转向模型的无模型深度强化学习框架，使 K1 人形机器人学习滑板运动。方法结合任务奖励与抑制投机行为的终止条件，限制失去支撑脚、双脚站上滑板、过度扭转、与滑板分离及滑板运动不稳定等行为。作者指出，这些约束在训练中的出现频率变化会形成隐式学习进程，使机器人从站姿控制逐步过渡到持续的人与滑板协同运动。摘要未提供量化实验结果。

sections.text:
Perceiving objects in the environment is a fundamental capability of autonomous robots. In dark or low-light environments, external cameras often fail to reliably perceive object positions and geometry; when visual sensing is unavailable, completing target search, recognition, and grasping through touch alone becomes a key robot manipulation capability.

This task must simultaneously address container-scale spatial exploration and object-scale fine-grained geometric perception, which is particularly challenging for low-degree-of-freedom parallel grippers.

However, a unified framework remains lacking for connecting container-scale spatial exploration with object-scale fine-grained geometric perception and grasping. To address this challenge, we present \textbf{GLoTouch}, a global-to-local haptic perception and manipulation framework built on a parallel gripper.

In the global stage, the gripper holds a passive long-reach probe, combining force measurements with known tool geometry to localize contacts and actively estimate candidate-object positions, coarse contours, and heights.

In the local stage, the robot sets down the probe and uses the bilateral visuotactile sensors on the same gripper to directly acquire local haptic observations, which are matched against a given target 3-D model without object-specific training. We evaluate the framework in both simulation and real-robot experiments. Source code will be open-sourced.

summary.en: The paper presents GLoTouch, a global-to-local haptic perception and manipulation framework for parallel grippers, intended to search for, recognize, and grasp targets without external vision. In the global stage, force measurements and known probe geometry help estimate candidate objects’ positions, coarse contours, and heights. In the local stage, bilateral visuotactile sensors acquire observations for matching against a supplied 3-D target model, without object-specific training. The authors evaluate the framework in simulation and real-robot experiments.
summary.zh: 论文提出 GLoTouch，一种面向平行夹爪的全局到局部触觉感知与操作框架，旨在无外部视觉时完成目标搜索、识别和抓取。全局阶段使用夹爪持握长探针，结合力测量和已知工具几何信息，估计候选物体的位置、粗略轮廓和高度；局部阶段放下探针，以夹爪上的双侧视觉触觉传感器获取局部观测，并与给定的目标三维模型匹配，无需针对物体训练。作者在仿真和真实机器人实验中评估了该框架。

items.title: GLoTouch: Global-to-Local Haptic Perception Using a Parallel Gripper for Object Search, Recognition, and Grasping Without External Vision

sections.text:
Tight-space navigation requires a robot to clear obstacles and stop inside its goal despite uncertainty. We present GeoDiff, a motion-program planner coupling original-goal stopped-set inclusion, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation.

An exact feasible-translation characterization guides repair; request-local reuse reduces repeated geometric work. We establish conditions for compiler equivalence and reach-and-stop soundness. Across 11,440 floorplan-derived jobs, GeoDiff certifies 61/139 tasks at 5-cm tolerance within 15 s, versus 44/139 for the stop-set baseline.

The strongest observed external certificate adapter certifies 13/139 tasks from 119/139 native routes, separating route availability from certification. On tasks derived from public BARN maps, GeoDiff certifies 202/270 at 5-cm tolerance for a Jackal-shaped body, versus 3/270 for the portal baseline.

Development analyses distinguish emitter savings from solver coverage, and 1,420 route-tracking episodes characterize the execution interface. These results show how terminal reasoning and proof reuse increase finite-budget certification coverage while preserving the original physical task and goal.

summary.en: The paper introduces GeoDiff, a motion-program planner for noncircular robots navigating tight spaces under uncertainty, with the goal of clearing obstacles and stopping within the target. It combines stopped-set certification, witness-guided terminal repair, and factored proof compilation; the authors establish conditions for compiler equivalence and sound reach-and-stop behavior. The abstract reports more certified tasks than the respective baselines on floorplan-derived jobs and jobs based on public BARN maps. It also describes an external certificate adapter, route-tracking episodes, and analyses of certification coverage under finite time budgets.

sections.text:
Artificial Spiking Neural Networks have gained remarkable attention in the last few years due to their proven ability in simulating biological neural cultures and producing similar activity and trends.

Nevertheless, whether they can be trained for humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility and robust performance at once remains an open question. We study this problem by proposing a biologically inspired spiking network, trained by different learning schemes and tested on the H1-2 Unitree Humanoid.

These schemes differ in how recurrent weights are trained.

Ordered from most to least biologically faithful, they are: a fixed reservoir mimicking an in-vitro neural culture, where recurrent weights are kept frozen and only a linear readout is trained, the same network but with its synapses trained by reward-modulated spike timing dependent plasticity and eligibility propagation, and finally backpropagation through time as a non biological baseline for comparison.

All schemes relied on distillation of a reinforcement learning expert policy with dataset aggregation. We show that e-prop reached 100% survival rate matching backpropagation through time, whereas both the fixed reservoir and the reward-modulated STDP, though the closest to biological cultures, plateaued at a much lower performance (~43.7% and ~11% survival).

We explore in further detail which trends a real culture could and could not produce until now. Finally we demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full size humanoid H1-2.

summary.en: The paper studies whether artificial spiking neural networks can support humanoid locomotion while retaining biological plausibility. It compares a fixed reservoir, reward-modulated spike-timing-dependent plasticity with eligibility propagation, and backpropagation through time as a nonbiological baseline. All schemes use dataset aggregation to distill a reinforcement-learning expert policy. The authors report that e-prop reached a 100% survival rate, matching backpropagation through time, while the fixed reservoir and reward-modulated STDP performed substantially lower. They also demonstrate brief bipedal stepping on a full-size H1-2 humanoid.
summary.zh: 论文研究人工脉冲神经网络能否在保持生物学合理性的同时实现人形机器人运动，并比较了三种循环权重训练方案：固定储备池、奖励调制的脉冲时序依赖可塑性与资格传播，以及作为非生物学基线的时间反向传播。所有方案都通过数据集聚合蒸馏强化学习专家策略。作者报告，e-prop 的存活率达到 100%，与时间反向传播相当；固定储备池和奖励调制 STDP 的表现较低。论文还展示了全尺寸 H1-2 人形机器人上的短暂双足踏步。

sections.text:
Nowadays, most AUVs utilize Doppler velocity logs (DVLs) and inertial measurement units (IMUs) to achieve satisfactory dead-reckoning results. However, the DVL bottom lock may not be available in some scenarios, such as moving over a soft bottom or traveling further away from the seafloor beyond the DVL's range.

As a result, the localization system solely reliant on the IMU data will experience significant drift. The relatively high cost of DVLs also inhibits multirobot or swarm operations. In this article, we present the results of using fully connected feedforward neural networks to predict vehicle velocity (surge, sway, and heave) for AUV localization.

Approximation functions for the vehicle velocities are derived based on the generalized six degree-of-freedom dynamic equation and kinematics, proving that they are suitable for feedforward neural networks with measurable inputs. The neural networks are trained using field data collected using an AUV.

An ablation study was conducted to investigate the impacts of hyperparameters, and the most effective models were selected using the Akaike information criterion. The selected neural network models are tested on three new sets of mission data collected on two different days.

The quantitative results show that localization using vehicle velocities predicted by neural networks yields lower averaged root-mean-square distance errors and standard deviation compared to the DVL-aided dead-reckoning method. However, the extent of this improvement was found to depend on ocean current conditions.

The promising results show that lightweight fully connected feedforward neural networks offer an attractive approach for inertial-based underwater localization when DVLs or their measurements are not available.

summary.en: This paper studies fully connected feedforward neural networks that predict an AUV’s surge, sway, and heave velocities to support inertial localization when DVL bottom lock or measurements are unavailable. The authors derive velocity approximation functions from six-degree-of-freedom dynamics and kinematics, train the networks on AUV field data, and select models using the Akaike information criterion after an ablation study. Tests on three mission datasets collected on two days show lower average root-mean-square distance errors and standard deviations than DVL-aided dead reckoning; the improvement depends on ocean currents.
summary.zh: 本文研究在 DVL 底锁或测量不可用时，利用全连接前馈神经网络预测 AUV 的纵荡、横荡和垂荡速度，以辅助惯性定位。作者依据六自由度动力学与运动学推导速度近似函数，并用 AUV 实地数据训练模型，通过消融研究考察超参数，以赤池信息准则选择模型。模型在两个不同日期采集的三组任务数据上测试，定位的平均均方根距离误差和标准差低于 DVL 辅助航位推算；改进程度受海流条件影响。

sections.text:
Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis.

In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption.

This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots.

Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications.

Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.

summary.en: The paper proposes a continuum-robot environmental contact friction model based on complementarity constraints and the Coulomb friction assumption. It aims to capture static friction and motion hysteresis that the authors say are not characterized by approaches focused on internal friction. The model predicts static and sliding friction, hysteresis, and resulting robot deformation; the authors state that it can run in real time. Experimental validation used a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot. Compared with a frictionless model, the friction-included model reduced maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm to 5.85 mm.

sections.text:
Humanoid behavior foundation models (BFMs) acquire diverse skills through large-scale motion imitation and massively parallel reinforcement learning, yet broad behavioral capability does not ensure precise execution across physical conditions.

Without distinguishing the underlying dynamics, policies may favor conservative compromises over environment-specific precision. We introduce ECHO, an in-context BFM that turns interaction experience into environment-specific control, separating general behavioral capability from dynamics-specific execution.

Mixed and Annealed Sampling first establishes a behavior prior in a single pretraining stage by balancing targeted practice with broad motion coverage.

Building on this prior, Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns structured dynamics representations from interaction histories to guide residual corrections to the frozen prior, enabling adaptation without test-time parameter updates.

Extensive experiments show that ECHO outperforms all baseline methods across diverse motions and physical conditions. Moreover, deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates whole-body teleoperation spanning extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, alongside payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control.

Page is available at https://mwondering.github.io/echo-bfm/

summary.en: The paper presents ECHO, a behavior foundation model for humanoid whole-body control that uses interaction experience to adapt control to environment-specific dynamics. Mixed and Annealed Sampling balances targeted practice with broad motion coverage during pretraining. Context Representation and Residual Adaptation learns dynamics representations from interaction histories and uses them to guide residual corrections to a frozen behavior prior, without test-time parameter updates. The authors report that ECHO outperforms all baselines across diverse motions and physical conditions. Deployment on the Unitree G1 demonstrates teleoperation involving extreme acrobatics and terrain interaction, as well as payload adaptation in manipulation and whole-body control.
summary.zh: 本文提出 ECHO，一种面向人形机器人全身控制的行为基础模型，旨在将交互经验转化为适应特定环境动力学的控制。其混合与退火采样预训练阶段兼顾目标练习和广泛动作覆盖；上下文表示与残差适应则从交互历史中学习动力学表征，以引导冻结行为先验的残差修正，无需测试时更新参数。作者报告，广泛实验中 ECHO 在多种动作和物理条件下优于所有基线。Unitree G1 部署展示涵盖极限特技、地形交互，以及操作和全身控制中的载荷适应。

sections.text:
Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background.

While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator.

To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact.

In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep.

We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity.

Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

summary.en: This tutorial presents complementarity-based rigid-body contact models for robotics, connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. It explains how complementarity encodes non-penetration and frictional dissipation, and distinguishes equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations that can introduce lift-off or creep artifacts. The article examines existence and uniqueness of motions and contact forces, solver selection among multiple solutions, and trade-offs among first-order and Newton-based methods, regularization, proximal strategies, computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity.

sections.text:
Underwater vehicle-manipulator systems distribute actuation across thrusters and joint motors. Whole-body model predictive control (MPC), rather than separate vehicle and arm controllers, can coordinate both to extend the workspace and exploit the system's full kinematic capability.

Doing so, however, requires a hydrodynamic model and derivatives throughout the prediction horizon. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) captures geometry-dependent forces and moments for such a model, but is too expensive to evaluate online.

We present a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model combining smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from CFD. It compactly represents velocity and acceleration-dependent loads and provides their derivatives in closed form.

These derivatives are propagated through free-floating vehicle--manipulator dynamics for whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control, jointly optimizing thruster forces and joint torques for reaching and continuous tracking.

Held-out CFD tests validate the principal translational-force and rotational-moment fields and the added-inertia response. The analytical Jacobians evaluate faster and avoid the step-size sensitivity of central finite differences. Closed-loop Stonefish experiments demonstrate whole-body MPC in an independent marine simulator.

By making geometry-dependent hydrodynamics directly available to gradient-based control, the model incorporates water forces and their sensitivities into motion allocation between the vehicle and arm, rather than treating them only as disturbances.

summary.en: The paper presents a differentiable analytical hydrodynamic model that combines smooth spherical-harmonic force and moment fields with a coupled added-inertia matrix identified from computational fluid dynamics. It provides closed-form derivatives used in whole-body trajectory optimization and receding-horizon control for underwater vehicle-manipulator systems. Held-out CFD tests validate the principal force and moment fields and added-inertia response. The authors report faster analytical Jacobian evaluation without central finite-difference step-size sensitivity, and demonstrate closed-loop whole-body MPC in the independent Stonefish marine simulator.

sections.text:
Prior work calls the high attention on the first and last action tokens of a flow-based VLA policy a radial action sink, and uses these tokens to set the execution horizon. In language models, a sink is a token with high incoming attention, a small value, and little effect on the output.

We test whether that profile holds, not the horizon rule, in one $\pi_{0.5}$ checkpoint on five RoboCasa tasks. The two endpoints receive 5.4% of action-key mass, 1.4 percentage points above their uniform share, and rotary positional encoding produces this excess: directly in shallow layers and through upstream action-token RoPE deeper in the network.

The endpoints do not fit the sink profile. Their value norms stay near the action-token mean in all 18 layers.

On 250 paired episodes, masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than 4 points, and replacing their value directions with those of another observation lowers it by 3.2 to 7.2 points across three donors, whereas the same replacement on two non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix lowers it by 28.4 points.

The token that does fit the sink profile on mass and value norm is the prefix BOS; on this checkpoint, zeroing its value raises success in two paired runs, by +13.2 points (95% CI [+7.0, +19.4]) and +6.0 points ([+0.2, +11.8]).

Inside the action chunk, a relative-offset routing profile estimated on other tasks keeps 75% of action-token spread and keeps closed-loop success on three held-out tasks (42.7% against a 38.7% baseline), while uniform or shuffled routing drops success to 3-4%.High attention mass alone does not tell what a token does.

summary.en: The paper tests whether the first and last action tokens in one flow-based VLA checkpoint fit the attention-sink interpretation, using five RoboCasa tasks. The endpoints receive slightly more attention mass than their uniform share, but their value norms remain near the action-token mean. Masking them or zeroing their values changes success by less than four percentage points across 250 paired episodes; replacing non-endpoint tokens in the executed prefix has a larger effect. The prefix BOS fits the sink profile. On three held-out tasks, relative-offset routing preserves success, while uniform or shuffled routing reduces it to 3–4%.

sections.text:
Scaling embodied interaction data requires a broad collection of usable tasks, yet specifying and validating each task instance remains costly. We present AgenticTask, an agent-based framework that expands existing task collections under human intent.

Its central representation links interaction requirements to object and part bindings, scene and robot configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria. A task-generation agent reuses interaction structure to construct supported variations and revises incompatible configurations using validation feedback.

A task-execution agent uses the same bindings and geometric records to select robot-supported skills and check completion against the original task criteria.

On RoboCasa, the framework builds the AgenticTask collection, saving 16,450 task instances from 20,323 construction attempts at a throughput of 166.97 saved instances per elapsed hour, with 62.26% of construction attempts passing the configured physical checks.

The execution agent completes approximately 38% of evaluated tasks, with successful cases spanning object placement, articulated manipulation, and sequential arrangement. Diagnostic analysis identifies improvement priorities in construction reliability, action selection, task-robot compatibility, and runtime integration.

Together, these results demonstrate task-collection expansion with measured construction productivity and concrete execution evidence, providing a foundation for subsequent interaction-data collection for embodied AI.

Its representation links interaction requirements with object and part bindings, scene and robot configurations, initial conditions, and completion criteria. Generation constructs variations and revises incompatible configurations using validation feedback; execution selects supported skills and checks task completion. On RoboCasa, it saves 16,450 instances from 20,323 construction attempts, at 166.97 saved instances per elapsed hour, with 62.26% of attempts passing configured physical checks. The execution agent completes approximately 38% of evaluated tasks, with successes spanning placement, articulated manipulation, and sequential arrangement.

sections.text:
We present Video2SwimFish, an automated pipeline and benchmark for building controllable fish assets from real-fish videos for underwater embodied AI.

Given synchronized multi-view videos of an individual fish, the pipeline generates a metrically scaled deformable mesh from a VLM-selected canonical frame, builds internal articulation adapted to that individual's morphology through a VLM actor-critic loop, and extracts a Biological Locomotion Manifold (BLM).

The BLM provides a low-dimensional action space bounded by real-fish motion. Compared with learning directly in joint space, it lets the individual swimming policy of each reconstructed fish converge faster and reach a higher task success rate.

We release two paired datasets: synchronized top- and front-view recordings of 120 individual fish across 6 species, and the controllable assets and individual swimming policies derived from them.

Because every asset is tied to the animal it came from, the dataset supports a benchmark that evaluates locomotion learning not only on task success but on fidelity to that individual's locomotion behavior. We evaluate on two tasks, 3D trajectory following and target reaching, and a case study in which a simulated BlueROV underwater robot captures the assets.

We further validate biological realism with a human study in which fish experts rate the simulated fish, as a complement to the automated metrics. We find that task success and locomotion fidelity do not necessarily improve together, and we identify faithful reproduction of individual animal locomotion as an open challenge for the community.

Project website: https://hangongchen.github.io/video2swimfish-web/

summary.en: The paper presents Video2SwimFish, a pipeline that derives individually controllable fish models, articulation, and a biological locomotion manifold from synchronized multi-view videos. It also releases paired recordings and derived assets and policies covering 120 fish from six species. The authors evaluate trajectory following, target reaching, and a simulated underwater robot capture case, and use fish-expert ratings to assess biological realism. They report that task success and locomotion fidelity do not necessarily improve together, and identify faithful reproduction of individual motion as an open challenge.

sections.text:
The success of manipulation policies is closely tied to the spatial relationship between the robot and the target object, as well as the task being performed, making the ability to adjust the robot's pose critical for successful execution. When the robot starts away from the task, such adjustments require coordinating navigation with local manipulation.

Jointly training these capabilities incurs substantial computational and data costs, while navigating toward a predefined goal pose limits the flexibility needed to adapt to task-specific manipulation requirements.

To address these challenges, we propose Learning to Move from and for Manipulation Policies (M4M), a framework that learns manipulation-aware mobility directly from pretrained manipulation policies.

By leveraging the hidden representations of the policy's action-generating network as dense supervision, together with a limited number of manipulation execution outcomes, we learn a spatially conditioned embedding that captures task-dependent manipulation success across candidate robot poses.

From the robot's current stereo observations, this representation estimates manipulation success at unvisited poses without rolling out the manipulation policy at each location.

It is further integrated into navigation policy training, while a learned handoff policy decides when to transition from navigation to manipulation, enabling the robot to move and manipulate in a unified, task-aware manner.

Across eight articulated-object tasks in unseen RoboCasa kitchens, M4M achieves 47.0% mean task success, compared with 26.5% for the strongest baseline and 19.2% for direct manipulation execution, and refrigerator-closing experiments show consistent improvements across four frozen manipulation policies.

summary.en: The paper proposes M4M, which learns manipulation-aware mobility from pretrained manipulation policies. It uses internal policy representations and a limited number of manipulation outcomes to estimate success at unvisited robot poses, then integrates those estimates into navigation training with a learned navigation-to-manipulation handoff. Across eight articulated-object tasks in unseen RoboCasa kitchens, the authors report 47.0% mean success, compared with 26.5% for the strongest baseline and 19.2% for direct execution. Refrigerator-closing experiments show consistent improvements across four frozen manipulation policies.
summary.zh: 论文提出 M4M，使移动机器人从预训练操作策略中学习面向操作的移动能力。方法利用策略内部表征及少量操作结果，估计机器人在未访问位置执行操作的成功可能性，并训练导航策略与导航到操作的切换策略。在未见过的 RoboCasa 厨房中，八项关节物体任务的平均成功率为47.0%，高于最强基线的26.5%和直接操作的19.2%；冰箱关闭实验也显示，四个冻结操作策略均有一致提升。

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation.

However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions.

To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target.

Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment.

TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction.

Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.

summary.en: The paper introduces TacInno, defining tactile changes unexplained by vision and executed actions as “tactile innovation” and using them only as a training target. A tokenizer conditioned on visual observations and actions encodes future tactile changes into discrete codes, which the policy learns to predict; no code module is added at deployment. The authors report average success rates of 87.5% on six simulation tasks and 70.5% on four real-world tasks, exceeding the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points. Ablations examine visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction.
summary.zh: 论文提出 TacInno，将视觉和已执行动作无法解释的触觉变化定义为“触觉创新”，仅将其作为训练目标。其编码器根据视觉观察与动作压缩未来触觉变化为离散代码，策略学习预测代码；部署时不需额外代码模块。作者报告，该方法在六项仿真任务中的平均成功率为87.5%，在四项真实世界任务中为70.5%，分别比最强视触觉基线高10.7和9.0个百分点。消融研究检验了视觉与动作条件、多帧编码及辅助代码预测的作用。

items.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action

sections.text:
Role allocation strategies in human-robot collaboration typically assign tasks to both the human and the robot, limiting the user's ability to take initiative. Furthermore, allocation decisions may conflict with the user's intentions, and the rationale behind such allocations may remain unclear, potentially reducing both acceptance and collaboration fluency.

The novelty of the proposed framework is that the human is left free to contribute to the task, while the robot is dynamically allocated activities through a cost-driven Behavior Tree architecture according to user-expressed preferences and behavior.

Explicit preferences are extracted from natural language instructions using a large language model, whereas human activity is monitored online through a Shannon entropy-based analysis of hand-object interactions. Furthermore, the framework can recognize anomalies in human execution and autonomously trigger corrective robot actions.

The approach was validated through a pilot study and a multi-subject experiment involving 14 participants. Results demonstrate the potential of such an allocation strategy for enabling intuitive and engaging collaboration without increasing the perceived workload.

summary.en: The paper presents a dynamic task-allocation framework for human-robot collaboration in which people remain free to contribute while a cost-driven Behavior Tree assigns robot activities based on expressed preferences and observed behavior. A large language model extracts preferences from natural-language instructions, and Shannon-entropy analysis of hand-object interactions monitors human activity online. The framework can also detect execution anomalies and trigger corrective robot actions. A pilot study and a multi-subject experiment with 14 participants suggest potential for intuitive, engaging collaboration without increased perceived workload.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种人机协作动态任务分配框架：人可以自由参与任务，机器人则依据用户表达的偏好和行为，通过成本驱动的行为树动态安排活动。框架用大语言模型从自然语言指令中提取明确偏好，并以基于香农熵的手—物体交互分析在线监测人的活动；它还可识别人类执行异常并触发机器人纠正动作。作者通过一项试点研究和一项包含14名参与者的多主体实验进行验证，结果显示该策略有望提升协作的直观性与参与感，且不增加感知工作负担。

sections.text:
Training vision-language-action (VLA) policies from demonstrations typically samples trajectory segments uniformly or relies on static offline data curation before training.

However, we find that demonstration data vary sharply in supervision value across temporal windows, and that each window's value to the policy evolves substantially during training rather than being fixed or captured by raw loss alone.

Motivated by this finding, we propose RefreshGrad, an online adaptive data-sampling framework that periodically scores temporal windows from the evolving policy using five policy-native signals and dynamically adjusts their sampling weights during training.

RefreshGrad focuses optimization on informative, learnable windows without altering the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost. Across ten LIBERO-Plus manipulation tasks, RefreshGrad boosts average success from 60.7% (Uniform) and 68.2% (FAKTUAL) to 76.1% under visual perturbations, and from 57.4% and 73.3% to 81.3% in clean scenes.

summary.en: The paper introduces RefreshGrad, an online adaptive sampling framework for diffusion-based visuomotor learning. It is motivated by the finding that temporal windows in demonstrations differ in supervision value and that this value changes as the policy trains, beyond what raw loss or static offline curation captures. RefreshGrad periodically scores windows using five policy-native signals and adjusts their sampling weights, without changing the policy architecture, training objective, or inference cost. Across ten LIBERO-Plus tasks, the authors report average success rates of 76.1% under visual perturbations and 81.3% in clean scenes, above the listed baselines.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RefreshGrad，一种用于扩散式视觉运动学习的在线自适应数据采样框架。其依据是示范轨迹不同时间窗口的监督价值差异显著，而且价值会随策略训练而变化，不能仅由原始损失或固定离线筛选反映。RefreshGrad 使用五种策略自身信号定期评分，并动态调整窗口采样权重，以聚焦信息丰富且可学习的片段，同时不改变策略架构、训练目标或推理成本。在 LIBERO-Plus 的十项操作任务中，作者报告其在视觉扰动场景和干净场景下的平均成功率分别为76.1%和81.3%，高于摘要列出的基线。

items.title: RefreshGrad: An Online Adaptive Data-sampling Method for Diffusion-based Visuomotor Learning

sections.text:
Robot foundation models are increasingly adapted into task specialists to expand their embodied capabilities.

Yet these capabilities remain fragmented across separate policies, and existing model-merging methods do not reliably preserve them during closed-loop execution: parameter-space alignment provides only an indirect proxy for behavior, while regression may fail to preserve behavior at states not covered by its calibration inputs.

We present Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), an execution-aware, gradient-free framework that consolidates robot specialists into a single policy. Across two complementary timescales, TCR collects calibration inputs from expert rollouts spanning different stages of task execution and from intermediate states within iterative action generation.

To account for representation shifts introduced by merging, TCR recomputes each block's input through the already merged blocks. It then uses each expert's computation within the block to form module inputs and fits merged weights to match the experts' linear outputs.

A two-pass calibration procedure further refines the merged policy using separate rollout caches while retaining the frozen specialists as teachers. The resulting model preserves the original inference graph and requires neither expert routing nor additional gradient training.

On LIBERO, TCR merges four $\pi_{0.5}$ specialists and achieves 77.83% success across 1,200 evaluation episodes, outperforming FeatCal, RegMean, and direct weight averaging by 9.50, 24.17, and 33.00 percentage points, respectively.

summary.en: The paper presents Trajectory-Calibrated Regression (TCR), a gradient-free, execution-aware framework for merging robot specialist policies into one policy. TCR gathers calibration inputs from expert rollouts at different task stages and from intermediate states in iterative action generation. It recomputes module inputs through already merged blocks to address representation shifts, then fits merged weights to match experts’ linear outputs. A two-pass procedure uses separate rollout caches and keeps frozen specialists as teachers. On LIBERO, the authors report 77.83% success over 1,200 episodes after merging four π0.5 specialists, exceeding the listed methods.

sections.text:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have advanced rapidly in language-conditioned robotic manipulation, yet existing benchmarks mainly evaluate gripper--object contact and largely ignore how objects interact with the environment through gravity, friction, inertia, and mass distribution.

As a result, it remains unclear whether current policies truly understand physics or merely interpolate from their training data.

We address this gap through the lens of dynamic extrinsic dexterity and introduce PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark in which a robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace.

PhyDEX contains 35K trajectories (143 hours) across nine tasks and 100 scenes, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects with static, multiple, and moving destinations.

All data are generated by a scalable, fully automatic pipeline that combines grasp generation, motion planning, and closed-loop throw optimization under randomized physical properties. We evaluate three representative VLAs, GR00T N1.7, DynamicVLA, and ForceVLA, and find that all achieve success rates below 3\%.

Our analysis reveals two key bottlenecks: limited robustness of pretrained models, which causes most failures before the throw, and physical blindness, as providing ground-truth physical properties roughly doubles success. Experiments on a humanoid robot and in the real world show the same failure patterns.

We hope PhyDEX will drive the development of physically grounded robot policies.

summary.en: The paper introduces PhyDEX, a throwing benchmark for evaluating physical reasoning in vision-language-action models. A robot must infer an object's mass, center of mass, and friction to send it to a destination beyond its kinematic workspace. The benchmark includes nine tasks and 100 scenes, with 35,000 trajectories totaling 143 hours, covering uniform, irregular, and dynamic-mass objects. Its data come from an automated pipeline with randomized physical properties. Three evaluated VLA models achieve success rates below 3%. The authors identify pre-throw robustness failures and limited physical awareness; providing ground-truth properties roughly doubles success. Humanoid and real-world experiments show similar failure patterns.
summary.zh: 论文提出 PhyDEX，一个评测视觉—语言—动作模型物理推理能力的抛掷基准。机器人需推断物体质量、质心和摩擦特性，将物体投向运动学工作空间之外的目标；基准包含九项任务、100个场景，以及涵盖均匀、不规则和动态质量物体的数据，共35K条轨迹、143小时。数据由结合抓取生成、运动规划和闭环抛掷优化的自动流程生成，并随机化物理属性。对三种代表性模型的评测显示成功率均低于3%。作者分析指出，预训练模型鲁棒性有限导致多数失败发生在抛掷前，且提供真实物理属性后成功率约翻倍；人形机器人和真实世界实验呈现相同失败模式。

sections.text:
Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail.

In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent.

Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation.

It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes.

Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

summary.en: The paper introduces AgentRoboCritic for action-level analysis of frontier multimodal language agents performing direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. A policy states a local intent for each action, and a critic evaluates outcomes and failure modes against it. The analysis reports closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, semantic grounding across varied scenes, and zero-shot manipulation, while identifying grasping, alignment, and uneven recovery as limitations. The critic is validated on 400 human-annotated actions; the authors also release 12,844 annotated actions and a fine-tuned open-source critic.

sections.text:
Precise grounding matters. It specifies which object is the target and where that object is, even in clutter and for tiny objects, and it has to be fast enough for closed-loop control.

Yet vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models (WAMs) take perception from general-purpose vision-language and video-generation backbones, which still fail in these settings. We introduce GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that generates points and boxes as quantized coordinates in a shared vocabulary.

Training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning with GRPO, using supervision from public datasets and dedicated data engines.

Against 44 baselines across 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, GroundingPI establishes a new state of the art, averaging 73.68%, above the larger GPT-6 Astra (71.54%).As a downstream visual backbone, GroundingPI improves performance on robotic manipulation and autonomous driving.

Across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms all evaluated backbones in all four out-of-distribution settings, with relative gains of up to 24.8% over the strongest baseline. On RoboCasa-GR1, GroundingPI trained with 50% of the demonstrations outperforms those baselines trained with 75%.Its mean open-loop L2 error on nuScenes is 0.296 m.

We systematically analyze GroundingPI's pretraining in scale and data composition. Grounding quality and downstream manipulation improve with pretraining scale, with generalization tracking perceptual gains most closely.

Analyzing the data recipe across these 11 perceptual capabilities shows dense grounding's substantial benefits for both, and OCR's potential as a catalyst for perceptual learning. These results support grounding as a perceptual foundation, and dedicated perceptual pretraining as a promising direction for foundation models of physical intelligence.

summary.en: The paper introduces GroundingPI, a 4B grounding foundation model that represents points and boxes as quantized coordinates. Its training combines multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO reinforcement learning. The authors report a 73.68% average across 34 grounding benchmarks and improved downstream robotic manipulation and autonomous driving. In four out-of-distribution settings across RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, it outperforms the evaluated backbones. Simulated scaling analyses associate larger pretraining with better grounding and manipulation.
summary.zh: 论文提出 GroundingPI，一种生成量化坐标点和框的 4B grounding 基础模型，训练结合多模态与空间预训练、监督微调及 GRPO 强化学习。作者称，该模型在 34 项基准上取得平均 73.68%，并提升机器人操作和自动驾驶表现；在 RoboTwin 2.0 与 RoboCasa-GR1 的四种分布外设置中均优于所评估骨干模型。仿真分析还显示，扩大预训练规模与更好的 grounding 和下游操作表现相关。

sections.text:
A central goal of humanoid robotics is for robots to perform the everyday work people do in homes and workplaces. Existing egocentric video datasets cover many of these activities but provide little synchronized whole-body motion data for learning loco-manipulation at scale.

We build Awaken-Human, which pairs approximately 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body human motion and covers more than 100 skills.

Building on this, we also introduce Awaken-HI (Humanoid Intelligence), a vision-language-action model for humanoid loco-manipulation that jointly predicts original human motion and retargeted robot actions through a shared action expert.

We show that loco-manipulation skills transfer more effectively from people to humanoids when human trajectories directly supervise the shared action expert. Increasing human pretraining data reduces held-out robot action prediction error according to an empirical scaling law and raises the mean success rate on downstream real-robot tasks.

After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, Awaken-HI achieves a mean success rate of 93.75% across eight individual tasks and outperforms GR00T N1.7 and $\pi_{0.5}$ in both individual and long-horizon evaluations. The same policy generalizes to objects unseen during robot post-training and to new pairings of familiar objects and destinations.

summary.en: The paper presents Awaken-Human, pairing about 50,000 hours of egocentric stereo video with synchronized whole-body motion across more than 100 skills. It also introduces Awaken-HI, a humanoid loco-manipulation vision-language-action model that predicts both human motion and retargeted robot actions. The authors report that direct human-trajectory supervision improves transfer, while more human pretraining data lowers held-out robot action prediction error and raises real-robot task success. After full-corpus pretraining and T800 adaptation, its mean success rate is 93.75% across eight tasks, with reported generalization to unseen objects and new object-destination pairings.

sections.text:
Flow-based vision-language-action (VLA) models are highly effective for generalist robot manipulation, yet their reliance on computationally expensive VLM encoding and multi-step iterative action generation imposes a significant latency bottleneck.

The resulting inference latency makes it difficult for robots to respond quickly, especially in dynamic environments. We address this limitation with RAVEL (Rolling Asynchronous VLA Enabling Low-Latency Control), an asynchronous inference framework that addresses the computational bottlenecks of both the VLM backbone and the action expert.

To reduce the delay from multi-step action denoising, RAVEL allows near-term actions to be executed after a single additional denoising step by carrying partially denoised future actions forward in a rolling buffer.

To avoid blocking on slow VLM encoding, RAVEL decouples VLM encoding from rolling action generation, allowing the action expert to operate continuously using the latest available VLM context, while a lightweight Fast Observation Pathway (FOP) directly conditions the action expert on current observations.

Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, RAVEL consistently achieves substantially lower response latency while maintaining the task capability of the underlying VLA, enabling high-frequency and responsive closed-loop control.

summary.en: The paper introduces RAVEL, an asynchronous inference framework for flow-based vision-language-action models, targeting latency from visual-language encoding and iterative action generation. It carries partially denoised future actions in a rolling buffer, allowing near-term actions to execute after one additional denoising step. It also decouples visual-language encoding from action generation and adds a lightweight pathway for current observations. Across simulated and real-world manipulation tasks, the authors report substantially lower response latency while maintaining the underlying model’s task capability.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RAVEL，一种面向流模型视觉语言动作系统的异步推理框架，旨在降低视觉语言模型编码和迭代动作生成造成的延迟。它将部分去噪的未来动作保存在滚动缓冲区，使近期动作只需再进行一次去噪即可执行；同时把视觉语言编码与动作生成解耦，并以轻量快速观测通路输入当前观测。作者报告，在仿真和真实操作任务中，RAVEL 持续降低响应延迟，同时保持底层模型的任务能力，从而支持高频闭环控制。

sections.text:
Adapting robot policies to out-of-distribution (OOD) settings with limited real-world data remains a key bottleneck to generalist robots. The multimodality and scarcity of robotics data lead end-to-end approaches to overfit and break under small distribution shifts.

Test-time adaptation can alleviate this by correcting frozen policies at inference, but most methods ground their correction in a signal learned implicitly from robotic datasets, making it susceptible to the same shifts as the policy it corrects.

Recent methods that instead exploit explicit spatial information are typically limited to coarse corrections, missing the nuanced, task-relevant motion most manipulation tasks require.

We propose VG-Steer, which corrects existing policies by transferring the nuanced motion of successful in-distribution rollouts, captured along meaningful geometric axes, known here as object-relational distance pairs.

VG-Steer leverages the semantic understanding of Large Vision Models (LVMs) and Vision-Language Models (VLMs) reasoning, which combines the task-relevant entity pairs and their object-relational distance projections into a single tailored visual-geometric guidance signal.

In a simulation benchmark, it efficiently corrects flow-matching policies under pose and task-goal shifts; on a real robot experiment, it widens the region of the workspace the frozen policy covers, more than doubling its success rate on cable placements one grid step outside the training positions, and steers a single-task policy toward objects it was never trained on while nearly eliminating object confusion.

Project website: https://arthurfenderbucker.github.io/VG-Steer/

summary.en: The paper proposes VG-Steer, which uses large vision and vision-language models to identify task-relevant entities and geometric relations, turning successful in-distribution rollouts into visual-geometric guidance for correcting frozen robot policies at inference. In a simulation benchmark, it corrects flow-matching policies under pose and task-goal shifts. In a real-robot experiment, it expands the workspace covered by the policy, more than doubles success on cable placements one grid step beyond training positions, and steers a single-task policy toward unseen objects while nearly eliminating object confusion.
summary.zh: 论文提出 VG-Steer，通过大视觉模型与视觉语言模型识别任务相关实体及其几何关系，将成功的训练分布内操作轨迹转化为视觉几何引导信号，用于推理时修正冻结的机器人策略。仿真基准显示，该方法可在位姿和任务目标变化时修正流匹配策略。真实机器人实验中，它扩大了策略覆盖的工作空间；对训练位置外一格的电缆放置，成功率超过原来的两倍，并使单任务策略能朝未训练过的物体操作，同时几乎消除物体混淆。

items.title: VG-Steer: Visual-Geometric Policy Steering from In-Context Aligned Abstractions

sections.text:
Physical AI requires models that understand spatial relationships and dynamic environments and translate observations into actions under limited onboard compute.

We present TuringPAI, a family of models for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for shared vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation.

TuringPAI-VL is a 0.65B model built on HybridViT-MLQ, which combines convolutional local aggregation with Transformer-based global modeling. Multi-scale Latent Queries integrate spatial features and observation history within the same visual Transformer, providing a compact, structured interface to the language model.

Training combines general vision-language data with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. TuringPAI-VL supports general multimodal understanding and improves quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B, while providing a shared initialization for the two downstream VLA models.

For autonomous driving, TuringPAI-Drive maintains all evaluated ADE/FDE metrics within 1.2\% of a full-token HybridViT baseline using the MLQ interface and achieves comparable aggregate scores in an in-house simulation evaluation.

Using XPeng Native Runtime (XNRT) on a single NVIDIA Orin-X SoC, TuringPAI-Drive generates trajectories at 12\,Hz in on-vehicle operation. For robotic manipulation, TuringPAI-Embodied achieves a 96.8\% average success rate across the four LIBERO suites.

These results demonstrate a shared vision-language foundation for driving and robotic manipulation under practical on-device constraints.

summary.en: The paper presents TuringPAI, a model family for on-device Physical AI comprising TuringPAI-VL for vision-language understanding, TuringPAI-Drive for autonomous driving, and TuringPAI-Embodied for robotic manipulation. The VL model integrates spatial features and observation history through multi-scale latent queries and is trained with geometric, cross-view, and temporal supervision. The authors report improved quantitative geometric perception over Qwen2-VL-2B. Drive achieves comparable aggregate scores in the paper’s in-house simulation evaluation and generates trajectories at 12 Hz in on-vehicle operation. Embodied reports a 96.8% average success rate across four LIBERO suites; these results reflect the stated model and evaluation settings.
summary.zh: 论文介绍面向端侧物理 AI 的 TuringPAI 模型系列，包括视觉语言模型 TuringPAI-VL、自动驾驶模型 TuringPAI-Drive 和机器人操作模型 TuringPAI-Embodied。VL 模型通过多尺度潜在查询整合空间特征与观测历史，并接受几何、跨视角和时间监督；作者报告其几何感知量化表现优于 Qwen2-VL-2B。Drive 在文中所述自研仿真评估中取得可比的综合分数，车载运行时以 12 Hz 生成轨迹；Embodied 在四个 LIBERO 套件上的平均成功率为 96.8%。这些结果针对文中描述的模型和评估条件。

sections.text:
We release all 3,718 episodes from the ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluation (arXiv:2607.24481), which contains 600 teleoperated demonstrations and 3,118 rollouts of seven imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies on 12 tabletop tasks, recorded on low-cost SO-101 arms; 73% of the rollouts are failures.

Every policy for a task was trained or fine-tuned on the same 50 demonstrations and rolled out on the same cell, so the corpus contains many policies' failures on shared tasks. An operator labelled every rollout successful, suboptimal or failure.

Each episode has three camera views, joint states and actions and is available on the Hugging Face Hub in LeRobot v3.0 and a reward-model format. This note documents how the episodes were collected and the limitations that could affect their use.

summary.en: This note releases 3,718 real-robot episodes from the ArmnetBench v0.1 evaluation: 600 teleoperated demonstrations and 3,118 rollouts by seven imitation-learning and vision-language-action policies across 12 tabletop tasks. The authors report that 73% of rollouts are failures. For each task, policies used the same 50 demonstrations for training or fine-tuning and ran in the same cell. An operator labelled each rollout successful, suboptimal, or failed. Episodes include three camera views, joint states, and actions; the note documents collection and limitations.
summary.zh: 本文发布 ArmnetBench v0.1 评测中的 3,718 段真实机器人操作记录，包括 600 段遥操作示范和七种模仿学习及视觉语言动作策略在 12 项桌面任务上的 3,118 次 rollout，其中 73% 失败。各策略针对同一任务使用相同的 50 段示范训练或微调，并在同一工作单元运行；操作员将每次 rollout 标记为成功、次优或失败。每段记录包含三个相机视角、关节状态和动作。本文说明数据采集方式及可能影响使用的局限。

sections.text:
Autonomous navigation in diverse real-world environments remains one of the greatest challenges in robotics. It demands both robust low-level motion control to handle diverse terrain and high-level reasoning to interpret environmental cues.

We present ROAM (Robust Open-world Autonomous Mobility), a system that enables legged robots to perform kilometer-scale navigation in complex alpine and urban settings.

ROAM combines the world knowledge of a Vision-Language Model (VLM), pre-trained on internet-scale data, with robust locomotion and local planning policies learned in simulation via reinforcement learning (RL).

The VLM provides common-sense reasoning and semantic interpretation of the scene, assessing risks, interpreting signs, and producing semantic labels with associated navigation costs.

An open-vocabulary segmentation module converts these labels into a dense, real-time risk map, which conditions two pre-trained RL policies responsible for agile locomotion and local navigation, effectively coupling high-level VLM reasoning with low-level physical control.

Real-world experiments showed the system's ability to autonomously navigate a wide range of complex real-world environments. The robot completes kilometer-long hikes with minimal intervention, interprets signs to avoid danger, and evaluates its environment to identify safe areas on which to step.

This work represents a step toward the reliable deployment of systems in unstructured environments. However, it also underscores the challenges that remain in VLM reliability and spatial reasoning, indicating that foundational models are a crucial component but not yet a complete solution for navigation in the wild.

summary.en: The paper presents ROAM, which combines an internet-pretrained vision-language model with locomotion and local-planning policies learned through reinforcement learning in simulation. The model interprets scenes, assesses risks, reads signs, and assigns navigation costs to semantic labels. An open-vocabulary segmentation module turns these into a real-time risk map that conditions two pre-trained policies. The authors report real-world experiments in alpine and urban environments, including kilometer-long hikes with minimal intervention. They also identify reliability and spatial reasoning in vision-language models as continuing challenges.
summary.zh: 本文提出 ROAM，将互联网规模数据预训练的视觉语言模型与仿真中通过强化学习学习的运动和局部规划策略结合，用于复杂环境中的四足机器人导航。视觉语言模型解释场景、标识风险和路牌，并生成带导航代价的语义标签；开放词汇分割模块据此形成实时风险图，供两个预训练强化学习策略控制运动与局部导航。作者报告，真实环境实验中机器人能在高山和城市环境自主完成长距离行走、识别危险标识并评估落脚区域，所需人工干预较少；同时指出模型可靠性和空间推理仍有挑战。

items.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
